cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, written for the choirmaster. It comes from when Nathan the prophet came to David after his adultery with Bathsheba. And every word of it, David says straight to God.

cards.question: After Nathan's visit, David turns to God. What's the very first thing David asks Him for?
David asks God for mercy. What does David lean on when he asks?

cards.text: Then David asks God to blot out his transgressions, wash him clean and cleanse him from his sin. Friend, that's not a rinse, that's the deluxe car wash with the hot wax AND the tire shine.

cards.question: True or false: David tells God he isn't sure what he did wrong.

cards.text: He knows EXACTLY what he did, and he says his sin is always before him. Like that 'reply all' you sent to the whole office by mistake, the one you see every time you close your eyes.

cards.question: Then David says who his sin is against. Who does he name?

cards.text: No excuses, no 'okay, but hear me out,' just this: he's done what is evil in God's sight. I've burned a batch and blamed the oven, the timer AND the weather, and David doesn't even reach for the oven.

cards.question: David owns what he did, so that when God speaks, God will be proved ___.

cards.text: Then David looks back. Way, WAY back, further back than Bathsheba.

cards.question: How far back does David say his sin goes?

answers.text: To when his mother conceived him
To when he was anointed king

cards.text: Then David turns from what he's done to what God desires. It's truth, and David says exactly where God wants it.

cards.question: God desires truth. Where does David say God wants it?

cards.text: David says God teaches him wisdom in the inmost place. Then he asks God to purify him with hyssop so he'll be clean, and to wash him.

cards.question: True or false: David says that even after God washes him, a little of the stain will still show.

cards.text: Nope: whiter than snow. That's whiter than my apron at the START of a batch, and friend, that apron does NOT stay white past the first scoop of chocolate chips.
Then David talks about his bones, the bones God has crushed. He wants those bones to rejoice.

cards.question: With his bones crushed, what does David ask God to let him hear?
Then David asks God to hide His face from something. What is it?

cards.text: So far, David's asked God to wash away what he did. Now he asks for something bigger than a cleanup.

cards.question: David asks God to create something in him. What?

cards.text: Create, friend, not patch. That's not scraping the burnt edges off an old cookie, that's a whole new batch, and he asks God to renew a right spirit in him too.
Then David asks God for two things NOT to happen.

cards.question: First, David asks God not to cast him away. Away from what?
True or false: David also asks God not to take His Holy Spirit from him.

cards.text: Then David asks God to give something back. I bet he remembers exactly what it felt like.

cards.question: What does David ask God to restore to him?

cards.text: He asks God to sustain him with a willing spirit. Then David looks past himself, to other people who've gone wrong.

cards.question: David says he'll teach transgressors God's ways, and sinners will ___ to God.

cards.text: I've lived this one. Once I came out of my funk in that junk drawer, I made it my job to show every scared newcomer around, because when somebody helps you up, you turn around and help the next one.
Then David uses a heavy word. He asks God, the God of his salvation, to deliver him from bloodguilt.

cards.question: If God delivers him from bloodguilt, what does David say his tongue will do?

cards.text: Then David asks God to open his lips, and his mouth will declare God's praise. I went years in that drawer barely saying a word, and now I talk so much my ovens need a vacation.
Now David brings up sacrifices and burnt offerings. In his day, those were offered to God on the altar.

cards.question: True or false: David says God delights in sacrifice, so a sacrifice is what he'll bring.
If not burnt offerings, what does David say the sacrifices of God are?
True or false: David says God will turn away a broken and contrite heart.
At the end, David prays for more than himself. He asks God to cause Zion to prosper. What does he ask God to build up?
A few lines back, God took no pleasure in burnt offerings. Once Jerusalem is built up, what kind of sacrifices does David say God will delight in?

findings.problem: Bathsheba appears for the first time and isn't introduced. David and Nathan each get a short description, but she doesn't.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke compares blaming the oven to David's confession. Then the punchline puts David in the comparison ("David doesn't even reach for the oven"), which blends the everyday image with the Bible setting.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: In Psalm 51:4, "so that" follows "have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight." The question links it to "David owns what he did" instead, which decides how the two things connect when the text leaves that open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story card says David wants his bones to "rejoice" right before card 18 asks what he wants to hear. "Rejoice" points straight to "Joy and gladness" and rules out "Words of warning."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card cites only Psalm 51:12. Its second sentence ("David looks past himself, to other people who've gone wrong") tells the transgressors and sinners from Psalm 51:13, so the citation should be Psalm 51:12-13.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The story card is only Papa Dorin's drawer anecdote. It tells no part of Psalm 51 and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: In the backstory, helping the can opener is what pulled Papa Dorin out of his funk. Nobody helped him up first. The line "once I came out of my funk... because when somebody helps you up" changes the order and adds a helper the backstory doesn't have.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: "In his day, those were offered to God on the altar" is a Bible fact from outside Psalm 51:16, which the card cites. It has no reference. The altar shows up only in Psalm 51:19.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The statement "David says God delights in sacrifice" is false at Psalm 51:16. But Psalm 51:19 says "Then You will delight in righteous sacrifices," so a baker could argue "True." The statement needs to be limited to burnt offerings or to that moment.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
